one_month_reasoning: The window effectively ends at the Fri 30 Oct close, because 31 Oct is a Saturday. Q3 2026 results are now more likely inside it than not (~65%). Hudbay reported about two weeks earlier in 2026 than in 2025: Q1 on 30 Apr/1 May and Q2 on 29 Jul. Aggregators list 28 Oct [21], and the call notice normally comes about three weeks ahead, so its absence on 2 Oct is not evidence against that date. Consensus of $0.36-0.37 [21] is a high bar against Q2's $0.28. Q3 does get the ~10kt of Peru concentrate shipped late from Q2 and LME copper ~$6.0-6.5/lb [1,14]. On the other side, gold is ~$4,190 against a Q2 realized $4,312 [1]. I expect a roughly in-line print, with the swing factor being any early Copper World DFS capex number, which as the skeptic I treat as a downside risk. The Sep 28 Snow Lake plan upgrade and an Oct-2 intraday print near $27.2 tilt the start slightly up. So I take a lognormal with median $26.35 and monthly sigma ~17.5%, which is a touch wider than round 1 because of the likely earnings event.

fair_value.method: Blend of SOTP/EV-EBITDA ($26.5, 50%), P/E ($24.0, 25%) and FCF yield ($27.0, 25%). It is built on 2027E EBITDA of ~$1.45B, adj EPS ~$1.60 and FCF ~$600M. Those use guided 2027 volumes cut for execution (150kt Cu against a 162kt midpoint) on a skeptic deck of Cu $5.6/lb and Au $3,800/oz, with 444.1M shares.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Operations: 2027E EBITDA $1.45B x 6.5x = $9.43B. Copper World 70% $1.40B. Cactus $0.95B. Attributable net debt ~$0.02B. 444.1M shares.

inputs_detail.derivation: Guidance is 140-184kt for 2027 (midpoint 162kt) and a 159kt average for 2027-28, +28% on 2026 [19]. I take 150kt, below the midpoint, because Copper Mountain optimization is unproven (BC costs ran $3.22/lb in Q2 [1]) and the LSIB judicial review of the New Ingerbelle permit is pending [22,6].
Spot is Cu ~$6.50 and Au ~$4,187 [14]. I take ~14% off copper for the refined surplus and record exchange inventories [12,13], and ~9% off gold.

I bridge from the TTM $1.27B, which was earned at a trailing-average copper price of roughly $5.3/lb and with Q2 sales depressed by the port delay. Adding ~25kt of copper at about 60% margin gives ~+$0.17B. Copper at $5.6 against the TTM average gives ~+$0.09B. Gold at $3,800 against TTM realized gives ~-$0.08B. Total ~$1.45B. At spot prices this would be ~$1.8B.

This is a mid-cycle multiple for a BB-/Ba3 producer, trimmed from 7.0x in round 1 because 2027 is now a growth-year EBITDA that already includes the volume step-up. The current EV of ~$11.6B is ~9x TTM EBITDA.

Mitsubishi paid $600M for 30%, which implies $2.0B for 100% and $1.4B for 70%. I add nothing for PFS copper-price sensitivity (+$0.6B NPV8 per +$0.50/lb [19]) because the DFS capex will exceed the 2023 PFS [1].
The deal was paid with shares worth $1,135.6M (FS note 4 [20]); the C$1.48B headline was in Canadian dollars. I take ~15% off for the acquisition premium and its early project stage [3].
Reported net debt is -$80.5M, and I add back Mitsubishi's 30% share of the $334.5M Copper World cash, which is consistent with valuing CW at 70%.
The Q3 consensus annualizes to ~$1.45 at near-spot prices on 2026 volumes. Guided volume growth adds ~15-20%, and my lower metals deck takes most of that back, leaving ~$1.60 on 444.1M shares.
Downgrades to hold/sector perform [3,17] argue against a premium multiple on earnings at high metal prices, so I use the middle of the diversified-miner range.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF $600M / 444.1M shares = $1.35/sh at a 5% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: From EBITDA of $1.45B I deduct sustaining and BC growth capex of ~$0.55B, cash tax of ~$0.24B and interest of ~$0.06B. Copper World early works are funded from the ring-fenced CW cash and Mitsubishi's $180M.
BB-/Ba3 credit with 6.125% notes. I use roughly the coupon less modest growth, unchanged from round 1.

bear.story: Copper falls toward $4.75-5.00/lb as the refined surplus and record inventories bite [12,13], and gold slides to ~$3,500. Copper Mountain misses its 2027 ramp, or the New Ingerbelle judicial review delays the pit push-back. The Copper World DFS shows a big capex jump, which raises equity-funding fears for Hudbay's 70% from 2028. EBITDA comes in at ~$0.95B despite more tonnes, and the stock rerates to ~6x.

base.story: Metals give back part of their gains, and Hudbay delivers most of the guided 2027 volume step-up. Copper World is sanctioned with a moderate capex increase, and the balance sheet stays near net-neutral. With peak-cycle earnings capping the multiple, the stock trades around my $26 fair value.

bull.story: Copper holds above $6.5/lb and gold above $4,000, and the full 162kt+ of 2027 copper arrives, putting EBITDA near $2B. Copper World is sanctioned with robust economics and the stock rerates toward the top of the analyst range.

thesis_break_reason: At ~39% below spot, $16 gives a ~$7.1B market cap, under 5x my haircut 2027E EBITDA with no credit for Copper World (~$1.4B Mitsubishi-implied) or Cactus (~$1.1B paid in stock). Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: copper sustained below ~$5/lb, a Copper World capex or funding shock that forces equity issuance, a failed Copper Mountain ramp or court-ordered halt at New Ingerbelle, or a Constancia/Peru disruption.

reasoning: Round 2 takes the supervisor's filing-backed corrections on board. The main one is that I wrongly held 2027 volumes flat: the March 2026 outlook guides 140-184kt of copper in 2027 and a 159kt average for 2027-28, +28% on 2026 [19]. I keep the skeptic's metals haircut (Cu $5.6, Au $3,800) but apply it to 150kt rather than flat volume, and I bridge from a TTM base earned at a lower trailing copper average than I had assumed. That lifts 2027E EBITDA from $1.25B to ~$1.45B. I disagree with the supervisor's ~$1.6B on a similar deck: it gives no execution haircut, while Copper Mountain has the worst cost record in the portfolio ($3.22/lb in Q2 [1]) and a live permit judicial review [22]. Cactus is re-based to $1,135.6M of shares issued [20], and Copper World cash is treated consistently, at ~$20M attributable net debt with CW valued at 70%. I also correct realized gold to $4,312. Q3 consensus of $0.37 [21] anchors the P/E leg at ~$1.60. On the skeptic checks, no new downgrade or short report turned up after the Aug-2026 hold rating. The Copper World legal challenges have mostly gone Hudbay's way: the federal suits were dismissed in 2022 [24], and an ALJ upheld the air permit [23]. The right-of-way case and the New Ingerbelle judicial review are pending with no ruling date I could find, so they are tail risks rather than base-case events. My blended fair value rises from $24.6 to $26.0, just under spot and below the supervisor's $27, because I keep the price and execution haircuts. For the distribution I use a mixture: 85% lognormal with median $26 and sigma 0.47, plus 15% with median $23 and sigma 0.75 for the copper mean-reversion and fat-left-tail case. That gives P(>=$26) of ~0.49. Research for round 2 was about 7 searches and fetches; the X/Twitter and major sell-side reports were not consulted.
